agentic-ai.summary: Learn AI systems that plan, use tools and complete multi-step work on their own, taught on live client work at techcadd {city} rather than from slides.
overview: Agentic AI is software that pursues a goal on its own instead of answering a single prompt. A language model answers a question; an agent decides what to do next. Give it an outcome and it plans its own next step, calls a real tool — an API, a database, a browser, code — reads back what happened, and repeats until the goal is met, the budget runs out, or it needs a human. Four properties define an agent: goal-directedness, tool use, memory and autonomy. This programme in {city} teaches you to build, evaluate, secure and operate systems with those properties.

The most valuable judgement in this field is knowing when not to build an agent at all. A deterministic workflow runs the same steps every time and is cheaper, faster and easier to debug; an agent chooses its own path, which is powerful but harder to predict. That decision framework is taught in Module 02, before you write a line of agent code, because recognising which problems genuinely need planning and tool selection — and which just need a well-written function calling an API — is the senior skill here.

The syllabus is a single ladder of thirty-three modules with exit points at three, six and nine months, taught with live client work rather than slides. Module 01 starts at Python from the first line, so no programming background is required going in. From Module 02 onward every session is agent engineering: prompting and structured output, tool calling and MCP servers, retrieval-augmented generation with citations, memory and state, graph orchestration with human-in-the-loop approval, then evaluation, guardrails and a deployed capstone. The six-month stage adds async engineering, model routing and self-hosted serving, DSPy optimisation, production MCP gateways, GraphRAG, durable execution, multi-agent systems, browser and coding agents, red teaming, and Kubernetes deployment with cost engineering. The nine-month stage moves from building an agent to owning the platform around it: CDC ingestion with ACL propagation, billion-scale vector infrastructure, A2A interoperability, an evaluation service, fine-tuning and reinforcement-learning post-training, voice and multimodal agents, AgentOps and FinOps, and governance mapped to the EU AI Act and NIST AI RMF.

cloud-computing.summary: Learn deploying and running infrastructure on AWS and Azure instead of a server in the office, taught on live client work at techcadd {city} rather than from slides.
overview: Cloud computing turns infrastructure into a service. Instead of buying and maintaining every server, storage system and network device yourself, you provision computing resources on demand, scale them as workloads change, secure them through policy, automate them as code, and pay only for what you use. Four properties define it: on-demand provisioning, scalability up and down with demand, pay-as-you-go pricing, and high availability built on distributed infrastructure with backups and redundancy.

The work itself runs on a loop — plan the workload, provision the cloud resources, deploy the applications, then monitor and improve — and four capabilities make a cloud engineer: compute (EC2, containers and scalable workloads), network (VPC, subnets, routing and security), storage (S3, EBS, EFS and databases) and automation (Terraform, CI/CD and monitoring). The most valuable skill is knowing which service and architecture a problem actually needs: not every application requires Kubernetes, multiple servers or a complex setup, and a simple one may only need a virtual machine, storage, a database and proper networking. Traditional infrastructure still wins where you need complete control over dedicated hardware, predictable workloads or specific compliance requirements.

techcadd's Cloud Computing Certificate Program in {city} is a single 25-module ladder taught in {city}, with exit points at three, six and nine months. Module 01 begins with Linux administration, and Bash scripting, networking and Git follow from the ground up, so no coding background is assumed; from Module 05 onward every session runs on live AWS. Stage 1 covers IAM, VPC design, EC2 compute, storage and databases, scaling and high availability, ending in a complete multi-tier AWS capstone. Stage 2 adds serverless and event-driven AWS, security engineering and disaster recovery, AI and generative-AI services on AWS, Docker, Kubernetes, Jenkins, Terraform, observability and AI model deployment. Stage 3 is a structured extension that deepens the same domains: architecture and resilience engineering, security and compliance, production AI service engineering, Kubernetes operations at scale, GitOps automation, site reliability with cost optimisation, and MLOps with a final expert capstone.

Month 1 begins with Linux administration, Bash scripting, networking and Git from the ground up, so no coding background is assumed; from topic 05 onward every session runs on live AWS. Every topic is specified the same way — the subject matter, the named tool stack used in labs, the production problem the skill solves, and a practical artefact for your portfolio — and you advance when a deliverable passes review rather than when the calendar says so.

3ds-max.summary: Learn 3D modelling, lighting and photoreal rendering for architecture and product visuals, taught on live client work at techcadd {city} rather than from slides.
overview: techcadd's 3ds Max Certificate Program in {city} runs three to six months and is built for architecture and interior design students, and for anyone who needs to present design work as images a client responds to. You start with the interface, modifiers and core modelling tools, then move into polygon and spline modelling for the geometry most interior and architectural scenes call for. Materials and UV mapping come next, followed by lighting setups and daylight systems, which is usually what separates a convincing render from a flat one. Camera composition is treated as its own subject rather than an afterthought. Rendering is covered in both V-Ray and Corona, then post-production in Photoshop, since almost no professional render ships straight out of the render engine. The final module introduces walkthrough animation basics. Work is done on real plans, often imported from AutoCAD, with a trainer reviewing each scene as you build it. You finish with a rendered portfolio, CV preparation and interview practice for 3D Visualiser, Architectural Renderer or interior visualisation roles.

overview: techcadd's RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) Certificate Program in {city} runs 3 to 6 months for developers who want language models to answer reliably from a specific set of documents rather than from memory, taught hands-on rather than from slides. The course opens with why retrieval usually beats fine-tuning for factual work, then moves through document parsing and chunking, embeddings and similarity search, vector databases and indexing in Pinecone and ChromaDB, query rewriting and re-ranking, and grounded answering with citations. A full module is spent on evaluation and hallucination testing, which most free tutorials skip, before the programme closes with production deployment and scaling using Python, LangChain, Hugging Face, FastAPI and Claude. You build one retrieval system across the programme, reviewed by a trainer at every stage, and finish with a working, evaluated application, a documented internship letter, and CV and interview preparation aimed at AI Engineer and RAG Developer roles.
